fatal_errors: The proposed grain-size mechanism does not reconstruct the target comparison between as-cast equimolar WTaTiVZr and commercially sourced powder-sintered tungsten.

It replaces the target W-Ta-rich/Zr-Ti-rich two-BCC-phase segregation and multicomponent strengthening/toughening interpretation with an unsupported claim that grain-boundary spacing is the governing variable.
The proposed 600–1200 °C tensile regime does not match the target room-temperature compression, room-temperature-to-500 °C indentation, and room-temperature scratch tests.
Evidence E2 does not support the predicted toughness ordering: its reported static toughness is slightly higher for the ultrafine condition than for the coarse condition.
Composition-preserving heat treatments are not guaranteed to vary only grain size; precipitation, segregation, recovery, texture, and grain-boundary chemistry can remain major confounders.
explanation: The response addresses the broad strength–ductility–toughness problem and proposes a reasonably falsifiable same-composition grain-size comparison. Its measurements and falsification rule are useful, although a single fine/coarse pair would not establish that grain-boundary-mediated dislocation dynamics governs the response without multiple grain sizes and direct crack-tip/dislocation observations. Scientifically, it is not a reconstruction of the hidden study: it omits WTaTiVZr, pure-tungsten benchmarking, dendritic two-BCC segregation, solid-solution/lattice-distortion strengthening, Ti/V/Zr-associated damage tolerance, and all reported quantitative outcomes. The baseline is underspecified, and the temperature and loading conditions lie outside the tested target range. E1 supports only a general strength–toughness trade-off, while E2 concerns another material and gives a toughness result contrary to the stated coarse-grain prediction. Thus the proposal is a testable alternative hypothesis, but its high-temperature and fusion-material generalization is weakly evidenced.
